To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

psychosocial factors are associated with chronic disease for 1st and 4th worlds indigenous peoples and African American people, with the strongest findings for mental rather then physical health outcomes.

psychosocial factors are associated with a range of harmful health behaviors and chronic diseases for 4th indigenous groups and African American populations, and that transcendental meditation may be a useful intervention for African American populations.

psychosocial and chronic disease outcomes are associated for 4th World indigenous peoples and African-Americans, and that stress reduction interventions may help to reduce the burden of chronic disease and psychosocial stress in these communities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the health of 4th world people and their communities.
the health of minority groups, which suffer from high levels of chronic disease and a high burden of psychosocial distress.
the health consequences of stress for 4th World indigenous groups and African American populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

stress is associated with a range of chronic diseases and harmful health behaviors for African Americans and indigenous peoples, but that there is insufficient evidence to determine the directionality of the relationship and that there is insufficient research on stress moderating factors, stress interventions and the role of stress in chronic disease causation.
psychosocial factors, particularly stress and coping, play a major role in chronic disease development and health behaviors for 4th World indigenous peoples and African American communities.

psychosocial factors are important contributors to health for 4th indigenous peoples and African American populations and should be included in public health and health promotion programs for these groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
psychosocial and cultural stress are important contributors to the development of chronic disease in indigenous groups and African American populations.

psychosocial stresses are important contributors to the high burden of chronic diseases among indigenous peoples and African American groups and that interventions that address these stressors are warranted.
the relationship between stress and chronic disease is complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health effects of psychosocial and other forms of stress should be examined in the context of minority group culture.
psychosocial factors are an important contributor to disease risk for indigenous peoples and people of African descent, but that more work is needed on stress and health for these populations.
psychosocial and socioeconomic stressors are a significant contributor to chronic disease for indigenous peoples and people of African descent.
